children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let's begin. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you some questions about your child.

**First question: How old is your child?**

The age of your child is important because:
- Children under 16 may automatically qualify
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over generally don't qualify

Please tell me your child's age, or if you have multiple children, let's start with one child at a time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me help you determine if you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 8 years old, he falls into the under-16 category. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now, the next question:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old, I imagine he's not in paid work, but I need to confirm this to proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's just 8, so he's still in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

This means benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit that would be claimed in his own name. Again, at 8 years old, this is typically not applicable, but I need to confirm that Alex is not receiving any such benefits in his own right.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a young child, so nothing like that applies to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now, the next check:

**Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

Again, since Alex is only 8 years old and in primary school, he wouldn't be in any type of apprenticeship. But I need to confirm this to proceed. Can you confirm that Alex is not in any apprenticeship program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's definitely not in an apprenticeship - he's far too young for that! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely! That makes perfect sense. Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we're moving on to questions about you as the claimant. 

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (for up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself and family
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Do any of these apply to you?** Most commonly, people simply normally live in the UK. Which situation applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live here in England with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now the next important check:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You mentioned earlier that Alex lives at home with you, which means you satisfy the responsibility requirement. Being responsible for a child means ANY of the following:

1. **You live with the child** (which you've already told me applies to you and Alex)
2. You contribute to the child's upkeep (paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since Alex lives with you, you clearly meet this requirement. Can you confirm that Alex lives with you in your home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now an important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any given time. This is important to check because:

- If no one else is claiming, we can proceed
- If someone else is claiming but you both agree that you should claim instead, that's also fine (the other person would need to stop their claim)
- If there's a dispute about who should claim, HMRC would need to make the decision

Is anyone else (such as Alex's other parent, a grandparent, or another family member) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**What is Alex's current living situation?**

- Is Alex in hospital?
- Is Alex in local authority care?
- Is Alex fostered?
- Or is Alex living normally at home with you?

You mentioned Alex lives at home with you, so I believe the answer is that he's living normally at home. Can you confirm this, and that none of the special circumstances (hospital, care, or fostering) apply?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - Alex is just living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, not in care, and not fostered.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the local council paying any money towards Alex's housing or upkeep? Generally, you cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child's accommodation or maintenance.

Since Alex lives at home with you and you're supporting him, I expect the answer is that the council is NOT paying, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm supporting him myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me proceed to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

**Congratulations!** You meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - At 8 years old, he's under 16 and automatically qualifies  
✅ **Alex is not in disqualifying circumstances** - He's not working, not receiving benefits in his own right, and not in an apprenticeship  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK  
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - He lives with you full-time  
✅ **No competing claims** - Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  
✅ **No local authority support** - The council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through your tax return
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### Apply Here:
👉 **https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim**

Do you have any questions about claiming or the process?
